A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhotoAgent framework, UGC-Edit dataset, and editing benchmark. Their readable text, figures, tables, algorithm, and supplied appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite the changed title and expanded visual results.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing comparisons, a 20-participant user study, reward-model evaluation on PARA, simulation-consistency measurements, and runtime analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative comparisons against Nano-Banana2 and Grok-Imagine.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same perception, MCTS planning, execution, evaluation, and rollback procedures. Removing the appendix's executor-routing explanation does not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions retain approximately 7,000 UGC-Edit training photos, the 1,017-photo editing benchmark, and PARA evaluation. The additional visual examples remain within the existing photographic enhancement coverage; no new dataset, domain, or task is established.

E2.justification: v3 adds Nano-Banana2 and Grok-Imagine as evaluated qualitative comparators in Figures 9–12. The comparator sets in the existing quantitative comparison and user study remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated metrics, user-study design, resolution comparisons, and MCTS evaluation budgets are unchanged. The new qualitative panels specify no separate prompts or settings that establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Figures 9–10 add visual case analyses of unnecessary background edits, subject alteration, and over-enhancement by the new comparators. Existing ablations, simulation-consistency tests, generalization analysis, runtime tradeoffs, and PhotoAgent failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The correlation-reporting practices in Tables 3–4 also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds six illustrated comparisons and associated qualitative findings in Figures 9–12. All numerical results in Tables 1–6 remain unchanged, including PhotoAgent's BRISQUE score of 0.6217 and user-study preference share of 42.0%.

T1.justification: The MCTS state/action notation, reward and visit-count descriptions, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Relocating the algorithm and redrawing its schematic introduce no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about autonomous closed-loop editing, exploratory planning, UGC-Edit, and improved editing quality. The new title and supporting visual comparisons do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: New captions interpret Nano-Banana2's unnecessary edits as lacking aesthetic guidance and emphasize PhotoAgent's restraint, content preservation, and atmospheric enhancement relative to the added comparators. The applicability boundaries and limitations in Appendix G remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 deletes Appendix C's routing categories, benchmark-based editor-selection rationale, and optional parallel two-editor execution details. The abstract also replaces the repository link with a project-site link. Planner and evaluator hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds PhotoArtAgent to the discussion of language-model-based retouching agents. The EdiVal-Agent citation and reference supporting executor routing are removed. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, author-name and affiliation text, related-work sentence, and several captions change, and one implementation paragraph is removed. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Four new multi-panel figures substantially expand the comparative visual presentation. Figure 2's trees and icons are redrawn, Figure 3 changes its filtering label from LLM-based to VLM-based, and appendix floats are redistributed. Existing visual results remain, including the failure figure renumbered from 9 to 13.

improvement.justification: Figures 9–12 broaden qualitative evidence, but their prompts and settings are unspecified, limiting the comparative conclusions. Meanwhile, v3 removes executor-routing details and fragments the evaluator explanation across several pages. With quantitative validation unchanged, the added evidence and losses in reproducibility and readability do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
